What is C++: C++ is a powerful, statically-typed systems programming language that extends C with object-oriented, generic, and functional features. It gives fine-grained control over memory and performance.
C++ Versions: Major standards: C++98 (original), C++11 (modern), C++14, C++17, C++20, C++23. Each adds features. Compile with -std=c++17, -std=c++20, etc. Always check compiler support.
Compilers & Build: Major compilers: GCC (g++), Clang, MSVC. Build systems: CMake (most common), Make, Ninja, Bazel. CMake generates build files for your platform.

// Single file compile
// g++ -std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra -O2 -o app main.cpp

# CMakeLists.txt
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.25)
project(MyApp LANGUAGES CXX)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
add_executable(app main.cpp utils.cpp)
target_include_directories(app PRIVATE include)
Project Structure: Typical layout: src/ for .cpp, include/ for .hpp/.h, lib/ for dependencies, tests/ for unit tests. Use header guards (#pragma once) to prevent double inclusion.

my-project/
  CMakeLists.txt
  src/
    main.cpp
    utils.cpp
  include/
    mylib/
      utils.hpp
  tests/
    test_utils.cpp
  lib/
  README.md

// include/mylib/utils.hpp
#pragma once
int add(int a, int b);
Namespaces: Namespaces prevent name collisions. `std` is the standard library namespace. Nested namespaces (C++17): `namespace A::B::C {}`. Never `using namespace` in headers.
Basic Syntax: Semicolons terminate statements. Blocks use braces. `//` single-line, `/* */` multi-line comments. `std::cout` output, `std::cin` input. `#include` for headers.

auto & decltype: `auto` deduces type from initializer (C++11). `decltype` yields the type of an expression. `auto&` deduces reference, `const auto&` deduces const reference.

auto a = 42;        // int
auto b = 3.14;      // double
auto c = &a;        // int*
const int x = 5;
auto y = x;         // int (const dropped)
auto& z = x;        // const int&

decltype(x) w = 10; // const int
decltype(a + b) d;  // double (promotion)
Type Deduction Rules: `auto` strips references and top-level const (unless you use `auto&` or `const auto&`). `decltype(auto)` preserves exact type (C++14). Template deduction follows similar rules.
nullptr & Fixed-Width Types: `nullptr` (C++11) is the type-safe null pointer. `<cstdint>` provides `int32_t`, `uint64_t`, etc. with guaranteed sizes. `size_t` for sizes/indices.
const & constexpr: `const` for runtime constants. `constexpr` (C++11) for compile-time constants. `constinit` (C++20) guarantees static initialization. `consteval` (C++20) produces compile-time only.

Arithmetic & Logical: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%` (modulo). `++`, `--` (pre/post). `&&`, `||`, `!` short-circuit. Compound: `+=`, `-=`, etc. Integer division truncates toward zero.

int a = 10, b = 3;
int sum = a + b;   // 13
int div = a / b;   // 3 (truncation)
int rem = a % b;   // 1

bool cond = (a > 5) && (b < 10); // true

int x = 5;
int y = ++x;    // x=6, y=6
int z = x++;    // x=7, z=6
Bitwise & Shift: `&` (AND), `|` (OR), `^` (XOR), `~` (NOT), `<<` (left shift), `>>` (right shift). Useful for flags, bitfields, low-level protocols.
Overloaded Operators Basics: Operators can be overloaded for user types. `operator+`, `operator<<`, `operator[]`, `operator()`, etc. Keep semantics intuitive. Some cannot be overloaded (::, ., ?:, sizeof).
User-Defined Literals: Suffixes for literals (C++11). `operator""_suffix`. Common: `std::string` literal `s` (C++14), `std::chrono` literals. Must begin with underscore for user-defined.

if / else: Conditional branching. C++17 added `if constexpr` for compile-time branching in templates. C++17 init-statements: `if (init; cond)`.
Switch: Switch on integral/enum types. Each case needs `break` or `return`. `[[fallthrough]]` suppresses warnings. C++20 added init-statement for switch.
Loops: `for`, `while`, `do-while`. `break` exits, `continue` skips iteration. Classic for uses init;cond;incr pattern.
Range-Based For: Simplified iteration over containers (C++11). Works with arrays, STL containers, and anything with begin/end. Use `auto&` to avoid copies, `const auto&` for read-only.
if constexpr: Compile-time conditional (C++17). Unused branch is discarded, not compiled. Essential for template metaprogramming. Replaces SFINAE in many cases.
Structured Bindings: Decompose tuples, pairs, arrays, structs into individual variables (C++17). Works with `auto`, `auto&`, `const auto&`.
Init-Statements: Variables scoped to if/switch/for (C++17). Reduces scope, improves safety. Combined with structured bindings for powerful patterns.

Declaration & Definition: Declaration (prototype) tells compiler about name/return/params. Definition has the body. Default arguments go in declaration. `void` means no return.
Overloading & Default Args: Multiple functions with the same name but different parameters (overloading). Default arguments must be at the end. Resolved at compile time.
Lambda Expressions: Anonymous functions (C++11). `[]` capture by value, `[&]` by reference. Generic lambdas (C++14): `[](auto x)`. `mutable` allows modifying captured values.
Trailing Return Type: `auto func() -> type` (C++11). Useful when return type depends on parameter types. `decltype` in trailing return enables complex type computation.
noexcept: `noexcept` declares function won't throw. Optimizer can skip exception handling. `noexcept(condition)` for conditional noexcept. `noexcept` is part of function type.
consteval / constinit: `consteval` (C++20) forces compile-time evaluation (immediate function). `constinit` (C++20) guarantees static initialization order. Both complement constexpr.
Function Try Blocks: Function-level try block catches exceptions from constructor initializer lists and function bodies. Primarily useful in constructors for logging/re-throwing.

std::string: Dynamic, safe string from `<string>`. Methods: `length()`, `substr()`, `find()`, `rfind()`, `replace()`, `append()`, `insert()`, `erase()`. Concatenate with `+`.
String Views: `std::string_view` (C++17) is a non-owning reference to a string. Zero-copy. Perfect for function parameters. No null terminator guarantee.
Raw String Literals: Raw literals (C++11) preserve backslashes and newlines. `R"(text)"`. Delimiter optional: `R"delim(text)delim"`. Great for regex, file paths, JSON.
String Conversion: Convert between strings and numbers. `std::to_string()`, `std::stoi`, `stol`, `stod`, `stof`. `std::stringstream` for flexible formatting.
UTF-8 Support: C++11 added `u8"..."` for UTF-8 strings. C++20 made `char8_t` a distinct type. `<codecvt>` is deprecated. Use ICU or platform APIs for full Unicode support.

Classes & Objects: Classes bundle data and methods. Access specifiers: `public`, `private`, `protected`. Constructors with initializer lists. `this` points to current instance.
Inheritance & Polymorphism: Derived classes inherit from base. `virtual` functions enable dynamic dispatch. `override` keyword ensures correct override (C++11). Base class should have virtual destructor.
Virtual Destructors: Base class must have virtual destructor to ensure derived destructors run when deleting through base pointer. `= default` for compiler-generated version.
Pure Virtual & Abstract Classes: Pure virtual `= 0` makes class abstract (cannot instantiate). Derived classes must override. Interface-style classes have only pure virtual methods.
Virtual Inheritance: Solves diamond problem where multiple bases share a common ancestor. `virtual` in inheritance specifier ensures only one copy of base subobject.
Copy & Swap Idiom: Provide strong exception safety for copy-assignment. Implement copy constructor and destructor normally. Assignment operator takes by value (copy) then swaps.
Rule of Five: If you define any of destructor, copy constructor, copy assignment, move constructor, move assignment, define all five. Or =default/=delete.
Move Semantics: Move transfers resources without copying (C++11). `std::move` casts to rvalue. Move constructor/assignment use `&&`. After move, source is in valid but unspecified state.
RAII: Resource Acquisition Is Initialization. Constructor acquires, destructor releases. Smart pointers, `std::fstream`, `std::lock_guard`, `std::thread` all follow RAII.

std::vector: Dynamic array with O(1) amortized push_back, O(n) insert/erase. Contiguous memory. Methods: `push_back`, `pop_back`, `emplace_back`, `reserve`, `shrink_to_fit`.
std::map & std::set: Ordered associative containers (red-black tree). O(log n) lookup. `map<K,V>` key-value, `set<T>` unique values. Iterate in sorted order.
std::unordered_map / set: Hash-based containers (C++11). O(1) average lookup. Keys need hash function. No order guarantees. `reserve()` for pre-allocation.
std::deque: Double-ended queue. O(1) push/pop at both ends. Non-contiguous memory (chunks). Slightly slower than vector for index access.
std::list & forward_list: `std::list` doubly-linked, `std::forward_list` singly-linked (C++11). O(1) insert/erase anywhere with iterator. No random access. Higher per-element overhead.
Container Adaptors: `std::stack` (LIFO), `std::queue` (FIFO), `std::priority_queue` (max-heap). Built on underlying container (default deque or vector).
std::array: Fixed-size array wrapper (C++11). Stack-allocated. Knows its size. Safer than C arrays. `at()` for bounds checking. Compatible with STL algorithms.

sort, find, transform: Core algorithms from `<algorithm>`. `sort()`, `stable_sort()`, `find()`, `find_if()`, `transform()`, `for_each()`, `copy_if()`. Work on iterator pairs.
lower_bound & binary_search: Binary search on sorted ranges (O(log n)). `lower_bound` returns first >= value. `upper_bound` returns first > value. `binary_search` returns bool. `equal_range` returns both.
partial_sort & nth_element: `partial_sort` sorts first N elements, rest unsorted. `nth_element` places N-th element in correct position, partition around it. Both O(n log k) or O(n).
accumulate & iota: `std::accumulate` (<numeric>) sums/reduces a range. `std::iota` fills with incrementing values. `std::inner_product`, `std::adjacent_difference`, `std::partial_sum`.
count_if & for_each: `count_if` returns count matching predicate. `for_each` applies callable to each element. C++17: `for_each_n`. `all_of`, `any_of`, `none_of` for boolean checks.

Function & Class Templates: Templates parameterize types and values. `typename` or `class` for type params. Non-type params: `int N`. `auto` non-type params (C++17). Template specialization.
Template Specialization: Full specialization provides specific implementation for particular types. Partial specialization for some parameters. Used for type-specific optimization.
Template Template Parameters: Template parameter that is itself a template. Allows passing container templates. `template<typename> class Container`. Works with template template arguments.
Variadic Templates: Templates with variable number of arguments (C++11). `typename... Args`. Pack expansion with `...`. `sizeof...(Args)` for count. Recursive or fold-based processing.
Fold Expressions: Unary and binary folds over parameter packs (C++17). `(... op args)` unary right fold. `(args op ...)` unary left fold. `(init op ... op args)` binary fold.
SFINAE & enable_if: Substitution Failure Is Not An Error. `std::enable_if` controls template overload resolution. `<type_traits>` provides type predicates. Largely replaced by concepts in C++20.

Concepts: Compile-time constraints on template parameters (C++20). Standard: `std::integral`, `std::floating_point`, `std::ranges::range`, `std::convertible_to`. Custom with `concept`.
Ranges Library: Composable, lazy range algorithms (C++20). Pipe syntax `|` for composition. Views: `filter`, `transform`, `take`, `drop`, `reverse`, `join`. `std::views` namespace.
Coroutines: Stackless coroutines (C++20). `co_await`, `co_yield`, `co_return`. Compiler generates state machine. Need library support (cppcoro, or custom promise/awaiter).
Modules: Modern replacement for headers (C++20). `export module`, `import`. Faster compilation, no header guards, better encapsulation. Not all compilers fully support.
Spaceship Operator <=>: Three-way comparison operator (C++20). Returns `std::strong_ordering`, `std::weak_ordering`, `std::partial_ordering`. `= default` generates all six comparison operators.
Views & Lazy Evaluation: `std::views` provide lazy, composable transformations. No allocations. `std::span` is a non-owning view over contiguous memory (C++20). `std::string_view` for strings.

std::expected: std::expected<T, E> (C++23) represents a value or an error, like Rust's Result. No exceptions needed. Methods: has_value(), value(), error(), value_or(). Monadic: and_then, or_else, transform, transform_error. Header <expected>. Useful for fallible operations where exceptions are banned or overhead unacceptable. Unlike optional, expected carries error info.
Deducing This: Deduce the reference qualifier of `this` for member functions. Allows lambda-like syntax for member functions. Eliminates need for const/non-const overload pairs.
flat_map & flat_set: Contiguous-storage associative containers. `std::flat_map<K,V>` sorted vector<pair>. Faster iteration, less memory, but O(n) insertion. From `<flat_map>`.
mdspan: Multidimensional array view (C++23). Non-owning, layout-polymorphic. Supports strides, extents, subspan. From `<mdspan>`. Replaces manual index calculation.

std::unique_ptr: Exclusive ownership. Non-copyable, movable. `std::make_unique` (C++14). Custom deleter as template parameter. Automatic memory management with zero overhead.
std::shared_ptr: Reference-counted shared ownership. `std::make_shared` allocates control block and object together (one allocation). Thread-safe ref count.
std::weak_ptr: Non-owning reference to shared_ptr. Breaks circular references. Lock to get temporary shared_ptr. `expired()` checks if object still exists.
enable_shared_from_this: CRTP base class that lets object safely create shared_ptrs to itself. Requires object is already managed by shared_ptr. `shared_from_this()` method.
Custom Deleters: Smart pointers accept custom deleters (callable). For non-memory resources: file handles, sockets, C resources. Stored in control block (shared_ptr) or as part of unique_ptr type.

std::thread: OS thread wrapper. `join()` blocks until completion. `detach()` lets run independently (careful with dangling). `std::this_thread::sleep_for`, `get_id`.
Mutex & Locks: `std::mutex` protects shared data. `std::lock_guard` RAII lock. `std::unique_lock` more flexible (defer, try, timed). `std::shared_mutex` (C++17) reader-writer.
Async & Futures: `std::async` launches async tasks. `std::future<T>` gets result once. `std::promise<T>` manually sets value/exception. `std::packaged_task` wraps callable.
std::jthread: Joining thread (C++20). Automatically joins on destruction. Cooperative cancellation via `get_stop_token()`, `request_stop()`.
std::latch & std::barrier: `std::latch` (C++20) single-use countdown. `std::barrier` (C++20) reusable synchronization point. Both from `<latch>` and `<barrier>`.
std::counting_semaphore: Signaling mechanism (C++20). `std::counting_semaphore<max>` with `acquire()`, `release()`. Binary semaphore alias `std::binary_semaphore`. Good for producer-consumer.
std::latch, std::barrier & std::semaphor: C++20 added std::latch (single-use countdown), std::barrier (reusable phase sync), std::counting_semaphore, std::binary_semaphore. std::latch: wait for N events. std::barrier: synchronize threads at a point, repeated. std::semaphore: limited resource access. All in <latch>, <barrier>, <semaphore>. Lower-level than std::async but more flexible than manual atomics.

std::fstream Basics: File streams: `ifstream` (read), `ofstream` (write), `fstream` (read+write). RAII: closes in destructor. Open modes: `app`, `binary`, `in`, `out`, `trunc`.
std::filesystem: Filesystem library (C++17). Path manipulation, directory iteration, file status. `std::filesystem::path`, `directory_iterator`, `file_status`. Cross-platform.
std::stringstream: In-memory string I/O. `std::stringstream`, `std::istringstream`, `std::ostringstream`. Works with `<<` and `>>`. Useful for parsing and formatting.
Binary I/O: Reading/writing raw bytes. `read()`, `write()` on streams. `reinterpret_cast` for type punning. Endianness and portability concerns.

Exceptions: Exception handling with `try`, `catch`, `throw`. Stack unwinding calls destructors. Catch by reference. `catch(...)` catches all. Re-throw with `throw;`.
noexcept Specifier: `noexcept` promises no exception. `noexcept(condition)` conditional. `noexcept` operator checks. Violation calls `std::terminate`. Optimizer can improve code.
std::exception Hierarchy: Standard exception classes from `<stdexcept>`. Base: `std::exception`. Derived: `logic_error`, `runtime_error`, `bad_alloc`, `bad_cast`, etc.
Error Codes & std::error_code: Lightweight error handling without exceptions. `<system_error>`: `std::error_code`, `std::error_category`. `std::errc` for standard POSIX errors.
noexcept & noexcept Specifier Deep: noexcept specifies a function won't throw. Compiler may optimize: no stack unwinding overhead. If noexcept function throws, std::terminate() called. Conditional: noexcept(expr). noexcept operator checks if expr is noexcept. Move constructors should be noexcept for optimal container performance. Essential for swap, move operations. noexcept is part of function type (may affect overload resolution).

CMake Deep: Modern CMake (3.x): targets, properties, generator expressions. `target_link_libraries`, `target_include_directories`, `INTERFACE/PUBLIC/PRIVATE`. FetchContent for dependencies.

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.25)
project(MyLib VERSION 1.0.0 LANGUAGES CXX)

# C++ standard
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 23)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)

# Library target
add_library(mylib
    src/core.cpp
    src/utils.cpp
)
target_include_directories(mylib
    PUBLIC include
    PRIVATE src
)
target_compile_options(mylib PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic)

# Executable
add_executable(myapp src/main.cpp)
target_link_libraries(myapp PRIVATE mylib)

# FetchContent for dependencies
include(FetchContent)
FetchContent_Declare(
    fmt
    GIT_REPOSITORY https://github.com/fmtlib/fmt
    GIT_TAG 10.1.0
)
FetchContent_MakeAvailable(fmt)
target_link_libraries(myapp PRIVATE fmt::fmt)

# Install
install(TARGETS mylib myapp DESTINATION lib)
install(FILES include/mylib.hpp DESTINATION include)
vcpkg: C++ package manager by Microsoft. Manifest mode (`vcpkg.json`). Integrates with CMake via toolchain file. Ports for 2000+ libraries.

# vcpkg.json
{
    "name": "my-project",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "dependencies": [
        "fmt",
        "boost-asio",
        "nlohmann-json",
        {
            "name": "imgui",
            "features": ["opengl3", "glfw-binding"]
        }
    ]
}

# Install dependencies
# vcpkg install

# CMake integration
# cmake -B build -S . -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=/path/to/vcpkg.cmake

# In CMakeLists.txt (after find_package)
find_package(fmt CONFIG REQUIRED)
find_package(nlohmann_json CONFIG REQUIRED)
target_link_libraries(myapp PRIVATE fmt::fmt nlohmann_json::nlohmann_json)
Conan: Decentralized C/C++ package manager. `conanfile.txt` or `conanfile.py`. Supports multiple generators (CMake, MSBuild, etc.). Profiles for configurations.

# conanfile.txt
[requires]
fmt/10.1.0
boost/1.84.0
nlohmann_json/3.11.2

[generators]
CMakeDeps
CMakeToolchain

[options]
boost/*:shared=False

# Install dependencies
# conan install . --output-folder=build --build=missing

# CMakeLists.txt
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.25)
project(MyApp)

find_package(fmt CONFIG REQUIRED)
find_package(nlohmann_json CONFIG REQUIRED)

add_executable(app main.cpp)
target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE fmt::fmt nlohmann_json::nlohmann_json)

Build Tools Overview: Ninja (fast parallel builds), Make (classic), Bazel (monorepo), Meson (Python-based). C++20 modules require build system support.

# Ninja (generated by CMake)
# cmake -B build -G Ninja
# ninja -C build

CXX = g++
CXXFLAGS = -std=c++20 -Wall -O2

app: main.cpp utils.cpp
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -o $@ $^

clean:
	rm -f app *.o

# Bazel BUILD file
# cc_binary(

Qt Framework: Cross-platform framework for GUI, networking, SQL, etc. Key modules: QtWidgets, QtCore, QtNetwork, QtQml, QtQuick. Signal-slot mechanism for communication.
Boost Libraries: Peer-reviewed, portable C++ library collection. Key: Boost.Asio (networking), Boost.Beast (HTTP/WebSocket), Boost.Filesystem, Boost.Test, Boost.PropertyTree, Boost.ProgramOptions.
Unreal Engine C++: UE uses C++ with reflection macros: `UCLASS`, `USTRUCT`, `UPROPERTY`, `UFUNCTION`. Gameplay classes, Actors, Components, GameplayAbilitySystem.
Google Test & Benchmark: Testing and benchmarking. GTest: `TEST`, `EXPECT_EQ`, `ASSERT_TRUE`. GMock for mocking. Google Benchmark for performance measurement.

std::optional (C++17): `std::optional<T>` holds a value or nothing. Avoids sentinel values (-1, nullptr, empty string). `has_value()`, `value()` (throws `std::bad_optional_access` on empty), `value_or(default)`. Monadic ops in C++23: `and_then`, `transform`, `or_else`.
std::variant (C++17): Type-safe union from `<variant>`. Holds one of several types at a time. `std::visit()` dispatches based on current type. `index()` returns which alternative is active. No undefined behavior unlike raw unions. `std::monostate` for empty variant.
std::any (C++17): Type-erased container (like `void*` but type-safe). From `<any>`. `any_cast<T>()` throws `std::bad_any_cast` on type mismatch. `has_value()`, `type()` for RTTI. Prefer `variant` when types are known at compile time.
Type Traits & Metaprogramming: `<type_traits>` provides compile-time queries: `is_integral`, `is_floating_point`, `is_pointer`, `is_same`, `remove_reference`, `decay`, `enable_if`. `static_assert` for compile-time checking. `if constexpr` (C++17) simplifies template code.

Inline Variables (C++17): C++17 extends `inline` to variables, allowing header-only definitions without ODR violations. Previously, static class members and global constants needed a `.cpp` definition. `inline constexpr` works too. All translation units share one address.
[[nodiscard]] & [[maybe_unused]]: `[[nodiscard]]` (C++17) warns if return value is discarded. C++20 adds `[[nodiscard("reason")]]`. `[[maybe_unused]]` suppresses unused warnings. Essential for error-returning functions, RAII guards, and stub/hook points.
std::clamp / std::gcd / std::lcm (C++17): `std::clamp(v, lo, hi)` from `<algorithm>` constrains a value to [lo, hi]. `std::gcd` / `std::lcm` from `<numeric>` compute greatest common divisor and least common multiple. All are constexpr-friendly.
Parallel STL Algorithms (C++17): Execution policies from `<execution>`: `seq` (sequential), `par` (parallel threads), `par_unseq` (parallel + SIMD), `unseq` (C++20, vectorized single-thread). Apply to `sort`, `transform`, `for_each`, `reduce`, etc. Backend: Intel TBB or compiler-specific.
Code Organization (PIMPL Idiom): PIMPL (Pointer to Implementation) hides private members from the header, reducing recompilation dependencies. The header only has a forward-declared struct pointer (`Impl*` or `unique_ptr<Impl>`). The .cpp file defines the implementation struct.
Design Patterns: Strategy & Observer: Strategy: encapsulate algorithms behind a common interface, selected at runtime. Observer: one-to-many notification on state change. C++ supports both via virtual interfaces, `std::function`, and smart pointers for ownership management.
Testing with Catch2 & GTest: Catch2: header-only (v2) or compiled library (v3), BDD-style with SECTIONs. GTest: xUnit-style, `TEST()`, `EXPECT_EQ`, `ASSERT_TRUE`. Both support matchers, fixtures, and parameterized tests. Integrate with CMake: `enable_testing()` + `add_test()`.
Performance Optimization: From Professional C++: 1) Move semantics avoid deep copies. 2) Reserve vector capacity upfront. 3) Pass by const reference, not value. 4) CRTP avoids virtual dispatch in hot paths. 5) Profile first (Google Benchmark, perf). 6) Small-string optimization.

References: A reference (`T&`) is an alias to an existing object. Cannot be null, must be initialized, cannot be rebound. Used for function parameters (pass by reference) and return values.
Raw Pointers: Pointers hold memory addresses. Declared as `T*`. Dereference with `*`, get address with `&`. Can be null (`nullptr`). Support pointer arithmetic.
new & delete: Dynamic memory allocation. `new` allocates + constructs, `delete` destructs + deallocates. Array forms: `new[]`, `delete[]`. Prefer smart pointers in modern C++.
Memory Leakage: Memory allocated with `new` that is never `delete`d. Causes: lost pointers, exception before delete, circular shared_ptr. Tools: Valgrind, AddressSanitizer.
Memory Model: C++ memory model defines how threads interact through memory. `std::memory_order` for atomics. Sequential consistency, acquire/release, relaxed.
Object Lifetime: Objects are created (constructor), live, then destroyed (destructor). Storage durations: automatic (stack), static, thread, dynamic (heap).

static_cast: Compile-time cast between related types. Numeric conversions, upcasts/downcasts in class hierarchies, `void*` to typed pointer.
dynamic_cast: Runtime-checked cast for polymorphic types. Requires at least one virtual function. Returns null for pointers on failure.
const_cast: Adds or removes `const`/`volatile` qualification. Modifying a const object through const_cast is UB.
reinterpret_cast: Unsafe cast that reinterprets the bit pattern. No type checking. Used for serialization, hardware access.
RTTI & typeid: Run-Time Type Information. `typeid` returns `std::type_info`. `dynamic_cast` also uses RTTI. Disabled with `-fno-rtti`.

Undefined Behavior: UB: program can do anything. Common: null dereference, buffer overflow, signed overflow, use-after-free, data races.
ADL: Argument-Dependent Lookup (Koenig lookup): searches namespaces of argument types when calling a function.
Name Mangling: Compilers encode function signatures into linker symbols. Different across compilers => no ABI compatibility. `extern "C"` disables mangling.
Macros: Preprocessor directives (`#define`, `#ifdef`, `#pragma`). Text substitution before compilation. Modern C++ prefers `constexpr`, templates.

#define PI 3.14159
#define SQUARE(x) ((x) * (x))
#ifndef MY_HEADER_H
#define MY_HEADER_H
#endif
#ifdef DEBUG
#define LOG(x) std::cerr << x << std::endl
#else
#define LOG(x)
#endif
std::cout << __FILE__ << ":" << __LINE__ << std::endl;
#define STR(x) #x
#define CONCAT(a,b) a ## b
Forward Declaration: Declaring a symbol before its full definition. Reduces compilation dependencies, breaks circular references.
Scope & Storage Duration: Scope controls name visibility. Storage duration: automatic (stack), static, thread, dynamic (heap). `::` for global scope.

Multiple Inheritance: A class can inherit from multiple base classes. Syntax: `class D : public A, public B`. Can lead to diamond problem.
Diamond Inheritance: Two classes share a common base. Virtual inheritance (`virtual public`) creates one shared subobject.
Virtual Tables: Each polymorphic class has a vtable. Each object has a vptr. `virtual` function calls dispatch through vtable at runtime.
Dynamic Polymorphism: Runtime polymorphism via virtual functions and base pointers/references. Enables substitutability.

GDB Basics: GNU Debugger: step through code, inspect variables, backtrace. Commands: `run`, `break`, `next`, `step`, `print`, `backtrace`.

# g++ -g -O0 -o app main.cpp
# gdb ./app
# (gdb) break main
# (gdb) run
# (gdb) next
# (gdb) step
# (gdb) print x
# (gdb) backtrace
# (gdb) continue
# (gdb) quit
Debugging Symbols: `-g` flag embeds debug info (DWARF on Linux, PDB on Windows). Levels: `-g0` none, `-g3` extra.

# g++ -g -O2 -o app main.cpp
# g++ -g3 -O0 -o app main.cpp
# objcopy --only-keep-debug app app.debug
# strip app
# nm -C app
# readelf -w app
Sanitizers: Google sanitizers catch memory errors and UB. `-fsanitize=address` (ASan), `-fsanitize=undefined` (UBSan).
Performance Profiling: Profiling measures where time is spent. `perf` (Linux), Google Benchmark, `gprof`.

# perf record -g ./app
# perf report
# g++ -pg -O2 -o app main.cpp
# ./app
# gprof app gmon.out > report

Compiler Stages: Four stages: 1) Preprocessing, 2) Compilation (C++ -> assembly), 3) Assembly (asm -> .o), 4) Linking.

# g++ -E main.cpp -o main.i
# g++ -S main.cpp -o main.s
# g++ -c main.cpp -o main.o
# g++ main.o utils.o -o app
GCC & Clang: GCC (`g++`): mature, extensive optimization. Clang (`clang++`): faster, better error messages, great tooling.

# g++ -std=c++23 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -O2 -o app main.cpp
# g++ -std=c++20 -O3 -march=native -flto -o app main.cpp
# clang++ -std=c++23 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -O2 -o app main.cpp
# clang-tidy src/main.cpp
# clang-format -i src/*.cpp
MSVC: Microsoft Visual C++: Windows-only, `/std:c++latest`. MinGW: GCC port for Windows.

# cl /std:c++latest /EHsc /W4 /O2 main.cpp
# cl /std:c++20 /EHsc /W4 /O2 /Fe:app.exe main.cpp
# g++ -std=c++20 -O2 -o app.exe main.cpp
# x86_64-w64-mingw32-g++ -std=c++20 -o app.exe main.cpp
# clang-cl /std:c++20 /EHsc main.cpp
Linkers & LTO: Linker combines object files into executable/library. Link-Time Optimization enables cross-TU inlining.

# g++ main.o utils.o -o app -static
# g++ -shared -o libmylib.so mylib.cpp
# g++ main.cpp -L. -lmylib -o app
# g++ -flto -O2 main.cpp utils.cpp -o app
# clang++ -flto -O2 main.cpp utils.cpp -o app
# nm -C app.o
# ldd app

CRTP: Curiously Recurring Template Pattern: derived class passes itself as template parameter to base. Static polymorphism, no vtable overhead.
Non-Copyable Idiom: Delete copy operations to prevent unintended duplication. Essential for RAII wrappers owning unique resources.
Erase-Remove Idiom: `remove`/`remove_if` moves elements to end, returns new logical end. Pair with `erase`. C++20 `std::erase` simplifies.
Copy on Write: Defer copying until a write is attempted. Less beneficial with move semantics.

std::chrono: Type-safe time library. `duration`, `time_point`, `clock`. C++20 adds calendar and time zones.
Random Number Generation: C++11 `<random>`: engines (mt19937) and distributions (uniform_int, normal). Better than `rand()`.

Iterator Categories: Five categories: Input, Output, Forward, Bidirectional, Random Access. Higher categories support more algorithms.

fmtlib: Fast, safe formatting library. Basis for C++20 `std::format`. Type-safe, extensible.
spdlog: Fast, header-only logging library. Async logging, rotating files, multiple sinks.
Protobuf & gRPC: Protocol Buffers: language-agnostic serialization. gRPC: RPC framework using protobuf + HTTP/2.
fmtlib & spdlog: fmtlib: fast, safe formatting library (format string syntax). Basis for C++20 std::format. Supports positional args, custom types, chrono. spdlog: header-only logging library, extremely fast. Levels: trace/debug/info/warn/error/critical/critical. Sinks: console, rotating file, syslog, daily. Pattern formatting, async mode. Zero-overhead when disabled at compile time.
